items.title: United Airlines Resolves Tech Issue That Caused Systemwide Outage
items.summary: Two major U.S. disruptions in four days add pressure on airlines and the FAA to show their systems can hold up heading into Thanksgiving.

items.title: Airlines Brace for Up to $1 Billion Hit From Ground Stop, but Holiday Demand Holds Steady
items.summary: Thanksgiving travelers have mostly shrugged off Friday’s ground stop. The four largest carriers haven’t been so lucky, facing up to $964 million in losses this quarter.

items.title: OpenAI Is Hiring Engineers to Build Travel Into ChatGPT
items.summary: OpenAI is getting serious about travel: Francis Davidson, formerly of Sonder and acquisition target Odessia, is now the AI company's very first head of travel. And he’s already hunting for builders to design how trip requests work in ChatGPT.

items.title: Airbnb Updates House Rules After Host Pushback
items.summary: Hosts got through to Airbnb on their complaints and Airbnb made changes. But most of the policies that stoked host anger, such as a limit on guest checkout chores, a ban on contracts, and collecting guest IDs, remain in place.

items.title: Another Hydrogen Passenger Plane Project Is Dead
items.summary: Cranfield’s exit leaves one fewer route to zero-emission flights for airlines, and for the island and regional routes where hydrogen was meant to arrive first. The industry’s net-zero plans still count on aircraft that their developers are walking away from.

items.title: MGM Dubai Slips to 2029, Handing Wynn a Longer Head Start
items.summary: MGM Dubai’s second delay in 18 months leaves Wynn even longer as the UAE’s only licensed casino operator. MGM is still holding space for a casino it may never get to run.

items.title: Industry Insights: Making Pet-Friendly Vacation Rentals More Profitable
items.summary: PetScreening founder and CEO John Bradford discusses how vacation rental operators can capitalize on growing demand for pet-friendly stays while managing property risks and improving operational consistency.

items.title: In Jordan, Arab Travelers Fill Amman While Petra Waits for the West
items.summary: Jordan’s tourism income is growing only because Arab and Asian visitors are replacing Western ones, and they are heading for Amman, not Petra. Until Western governments lift their travel warnings, the sites Jordan built its tourism on will keep struggling.
